title: Tourte Lorraine
subtitle: A double-crust pork and veal pie marinated in wine from the Lorraine region
excerpt: Strips of pork and veal marinated overnight in white wine and herbs, then baked in a double-crust pastry case with a cream and egg filling. A serious, impressive pie.
sourceNotes: Traditional pie from the Lorraine region of north-eastern France.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the baked pie whole, well wrapped. Thaw overnight in the fridge and reheat at 180C for 20 minutes.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The meat must marinate for at least 8 hours or overnight. The assembled uncooked pie can be refrigerated for up to 12 hours before baking.

content.text: Tourte Lorraine is a meat pie with a rich cream filling poured in through a hole in the lid. The marinade is part of the flavour, so do not skip it. Start the recipe the day before you plan to eat.
Combine the pork, veal, wine, shallots, thyme, parsley, bay leaves, salt, and pepper in a bowl. Cover and refrigerate for at least 8 hours or overnight.
Heat the oven to 200C. Drain the meat and discard the herbs and bay. Pat the meat dry with kitchen paper.
Roll two thirds of the pastry to 3mm thick. Line a 23cm pie dish, leaving some overhang. Arrange the drained meat in the case in an even layer.
Roll the remaining pastry for a lid. Brush the rim with beaten egg. Lay the lid over the filling and press the edges to seal. Trim and crimp.
Cut a small round hole in the centre of the lid, about 2cm across. Brush the surface all over with beaten egg.
Bake for 30 minutes until the pastry is deep gold. Remove from the oven.

Whisk the cream, remaining beaten egg, and nutmeg together. Using a small funnel or jug, pour the cream mixture through the hole in the lid. Return to the oven for 20 to 25 minutes until the filling is set. Rest for 15 minutes before cutting.

items.symptom: The cream filling leaks out of the hole.
items.cause: The hole was too large or the seal around the rim failed.
items.fix: Keep the hole small and use a makeshift foil funnel to pour in a controlled stream.

items.symptom: The pastry lid is pale after 30 minutes.
items.cause: The egg wash was thin or the oven is running cool.
items.fix: Apply a second coat of egg wash and raise the oven to 210C for the final 5 minutes.

items.symptom: The meat is dry and tough.
items.cause: The veal and pork were cut too thick or over-marinated without acid.
items.fix: Keep the strips to 1cm and check that the wine in the marinade is dry rather than sweet.
